question: Two identical circles each of radius 30 cm intersect each other such that the circumference of each one passes through the centre of the other. What is the area of the intersecting region?
solution:
**Given:**

Two identical circles each of radius 30 cm intersect each other such that the circumference of each one passes through the centre of the other.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c8dd6385fc5d23d2167c2ab302a2df5cee60f711699a38ebc787402d648bea3.png] 

OA = O’A = OB = OB’ = OO’ = 30 cm

In triangle AOO’,

OA = O’A = OO’ = 30 cm ( As all three sides of AOO' are equal so it is an equilateral triangle)

⇒ ∠AOO’ = 60°

⇒ ∠AOB = 120°

In triangle ACO,

AC² = OA² - OC² = 900 - 225

⇒ AC2 = 675

⇒ AC = 15√3

So, AB = 30√3

Area of AO’BA = Area of sector AO’BO - Area of triangle AOB =

⇒ π(30)² ÷ 3 - ½ ⨯ 30√3 ⨯ 15

⇒ 900π ÷ 3 - 225√3

⇒ 300π - 225√3

Area of intersecting region = 2(Area of AO’BA)

⇒ 600π - 450√3 cm² 

**∴ The required answer is 600π - 450√3 **cm2.
